message: Quitting smoking is the single biggest thing you can do for your longevity — risk starts falling within weeks and keeps falling for years.
Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week — even a brisk daily walk measurably lowers mortality risk.
Keeping blood pressure controlled — through medication and lifestyle — is one of the most effective ways to protect your lifespan.
Keeping diabetes well-managed (glucose, weight, activity) substantially reduces its impact on longevity.
Reducing central fat (waist circumference) lowers mortality risk more than body weight alone — modest, sustained loss helps.
Managing a respiratory condition (treatment adherence, avoiding smoke and polluted air) protects lung function and longevity.
Current evidence finds no safe level of alcohol — cutting down from moderate or heavy drinking lowers your risk, and every step down helps.
Moving toward a Mediterranean-style pattern — more vegetables, fruit, whole grains and fish, less red and processed meat — is one of the best-evidenced dietary changes for longevity.
Long daily sitting time carries risk of its own, even for people who exercise — breaking it up and trimming total hours both help.

Your answers suggest a high level of perceived stress lately. Stress-management routines (movement, sleep, social contact, or professional support) are worth prioritising — the mortality link is weaker than for smoking or diet, but your wellbeing matters either way.
